_notes: HIGH CONFIDENCE: Danish/German musical convention swaps H and B relative to English - Danish 'H' = English 'B' (natural), Danish 'B' = English 'Bb' (flat). This is NOT a translation error, it's the actual Danish/German note-naming tradition. Getting this backwards would be a real false-friend trap, same shape as the unit-conversion traps in ovos-skill-convert.

LOWER CONFIDENCE: the exact spelling of sharp/flat suffixes (ciss vs cis, ess vs es, the German-style contractions for As/Es) is a first pass, not verified against an authoritative Danish source - both plausible spellings are included below as aliases to hedge, pending review by someone who actually reads Danish sheet music.
